PROTESTA PACIFICA A TORINO, LA RIVOLTA DELLA POLIZIA CONTRO IL GOVERNO E IL SILENZIO DEI TG DI REGIME

​🚨 La massiccia mobilitazione pacifica che ha invaso Torino e le principali città d'Italia riceve il consueto trattamento dalla stampa asservita al potere: il silenzio e la censura dei telegiornali nazionali, pronti a fare sciacallaggio sulle tensioni ma del tutto ciechi di fronte a manifestazioni imponenti, civili e prive di scontri. In piazza una convergenza straordinaria di lavoratori, studenti, insegnanti ed agricoltori, che hanno dato vita ad azioni simboliche di grande impatto, come il rogo collettivo delle bollette per denunciare i costi energetici più alti d'Europa e la speculazione che affama le famiglie. Ma la vera scossa per i palazzi arriva dal fronte delle forze dell'ordine: gli stessi agenti di polizia si ribellano al governo Meloni e al ministro Piantedosi, accusandoli di aver tradito gli impegni solenni presi sulla previdenza dedicata, azzerata tra le pieghe dell'ultima manovra di bilancio. Con la proclamazione dello sciopero generale del 20 novembre, i sindacati di polizia annunciano di essere pronti ad abbassare gli scudi per schierarsi al fianco dei cittadini e dei lavoratori in mobilitazione. Quando persino chi indossa la divisa comprende di essere stato usato per coprire i fallimenti della politica, la propaganda di regime trema. Dalla rabbia degli agricoltori alla lotta sociale diffusa, il Paese reale rifiuta il funerale della democrazia e pretende la cacciata di chi affama il popolo! Condividete!

snippet.title: 10 Everyday Superfoods You Should Know About
snippet.description:
Do you eat these everyday foods without knowing how nutritious they really are? Your kitchen may already have some amazing ingredients packed with fiber, plant-based protein, vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants. Here are 10 foods worth adding to your balanced diet. Don't miss number 10!

Number 1. Sprouted Mung Beans: A great source of plant-based protein and fiber. Add them to salads or enjoy them as a light breakfast.

Number 2. Water Chestnuts: Contain carbohydrates, fiber, and essential minerals. They make a filling addition to your meals and snacks.

Number 3. Kiwi: Packed with vitamin C and fiber, this sweet-and-tangy fruit is a nutritious addition to your fruit bowl.

Number 4. Black Chickpeas: Provide plant-based protein and fiber, making boiled black chickpeas a satisfying snack.

Number 5. Fenugreek Leaves: Rich in fiber and several micronutrients. Add these leafy greens to your everyday meals for more variety.

Number 6. Oatmeal: Contains soluble fiber, including beta-glucan, which supports heart health. Choose plain oats and add your favorite toppings.

Number 7. Hazelnuts: Provide healthy fats, fiber, vitamin E, and other nutrients. Enjoy a small portion of unsalted hazelnuts.

Number 8. Eggplant: An affordable vegetable containing fiber and beneficial plant compounds. It can be prepared in many delicious ways.

Number 9. Bitter Gourd: Provides fiber, vitamin C, and other micronutrients. Its distinctive bitter taste adds variety to your vegetable choices.

Number 10. Urad Dal (Black Gram): A nutritious source of plant-based protein, fiber, and beneficial plant compounds. Include it in your meals for added nutritional variety.

snippet.title: Lal Bahadur Shastri: The 1965 War and the March Towards Lahore | Sattadhish Ep 19
snippet.description:
A freedom fighter was in a British jail when word came that his eldest daughter, Manju, was gravely ill. He could have parole, but only if he signed a promise to stay out of politics while he was outside. He refused. The jail superintendent let him go for fifteen days anyway. His daughter died the day he reached home. He performed her last rites and went straight back to jail, leaving the rest of his parole unused. Nobody then imagined that this prisoner would one day become India’s Prime Minister, or that when he died he would leave behind no property, only a bank loan.

Why did a young boy go on a hunger strike over a pigeon? Why did he drop the surname ‘Varma’ at the age of twelve? Why did he accept only a charkha and some khadi as dowry? Why did he resign as Railway Minister after a train accident he had nothing to do with? How did a single news agency report settle who would succeed Nehru? Why was no dinner cooked at the Prime Minister’s house on Monday evenings? What happened in Tashkent on the night of 10–11 January 1966? And which couplet did Shastri write on a piece of paper on his last morning?

In this episode of Sattadhish, Bhupinder Soni tells the full story of Lal Bahadur Shastri: his childhood in Mughalsarai and Benares, the Non-Cooperation Movement and Kashi Vidyapith, seven spells in jail, his years as a minister in Uttar Pradesh, his railway resignation, the Home Ministry and the Kamaraj Plan, the race to succeed Nehru, the 1965 war with Pakistan, ‘Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan’ and the Monday fast, the Tashkent Agreement, the questions that still surround his death, and the Fiat he bought with a Rs 5,000 loan from Punjab National Bank. The episode draws on C. P. Srivastava’s biography ‘Lal Bahadur Shastri: A Life of Truth in Politics’, Kuldip Nayar’s memoir ‘Beyond the Lines’, Sanjeev Chopra’s ‘The Great Conciliator’ and Anuj Dhar’s ‘Your Prime Minister Is Dead’.
